name: Eloralintide
lead: Eloralintide (LY3841136) is an investigational once-weekly selective amylin receptor agonist from Eli Lilly for obesity.[1][3] It is not approved.[1]

A 48-week phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight and a comorbidity was published in The Lancet in 2025.[2] Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports weight loss ranging from 9.5 percent at the lowest dose to 20.1 percent at the highest, versus 0.4 percent with placebo, with nausea and other gastrointestinal effects the most common adverse events.[1] Lilly began phase 3 trials in December 2025.[1][6]

paras: Eloralintide is described as selectively activating the amylin 1 receptor, slowing gastric emptying and promoting satiety; a fatty diacid chain extends its half-life, which Grokipedia reports as about 13 to 15 days in phase 1.[1][3]

Grokipedia reports mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal effects, mostly nausea, mostly during dose escalation, with fatigue in some dose groups and about 10 percent overall discontinuation similar to placebo.[1]

A 12-week phase 1 multiple ascending dose study and translational work in animals and humans have been published.[3][4] The 48-week phase 2 trial evaluated several doses and escalation schemes against placebo.[2] Phase 3 trials are enrolling participants with obesity, obesity with type 2 diabetes, and persistent obesity on a weekly incretin, and a phase 1 study combines it with tirzepatide.[5][6][7] A network meta-analysis and reviews place amylin agonists as an emerging class.[8][9]

timeline.event: Phase 2 results published in the Lancet; phase 3 begins in December.[1][2]

quick.overview:
Eloralintide is a weekly injectable amylin agonist from Eli Lilly. Phase 2 results appeared in the Lancet in 2025 and phase 3 trials are underway.

An AI-generated source reports 9.5 to 20.1 percent weight loss at 48 weeks.
quick.mechanism: It selectively activates the amylin receptor, promoting fullness and slowing stomach emptying.
quick.risks: Nausea and other gastrointestinal effects were most common. Not approved.
